description.value: Bucky's Taphouse is a long-established neighbourhood pub in Langford that explicitly courts cyclists rolling off the nearby Galloping Goose Regional Trail. It offers an extensive menu of wings, burgers, poutine, and appies alongside a sunny west-facing patio the website bills as 'the sunniest patio on the West Shore.' The spot has served the community for over 40 years and has been under its current kitchen direction since 2013.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website fully loaded and confirms Bucky's Taphouse is a functioning pub at 2668 Sooke Road, Langford BC, with matching phone and address to OSM. The homepage explicitly calls out Galloping Goose Trail cyclists ('just hopping off the Galloping Goose Trail, you'll feel right at home'), making this directly relevant to touring cyclists; no bike parking, washroom, or Wi-Fi amenities are explicitly described. Several menu items are flagged '(V)' suggesting vegetarian options, though the marker is inconsistently applied (some beef/bacon dishes also carry it).
concerns: OSM community field lists 'Victoria' but the business website consistently describes itself as being in 'Langford, BC' (a distinct municipality within Greater Victoria).
OSM opening_hours tag includes 'Su, Tu 00:00-24:00' (implying 24-hour operation) which contradicts the website showing 11am–9pm for both those days; the OSM hours tag appears erroneous.
Menu '(V)' vegetarian marker is applied inconsistently — appears on some beef/bacon dishes — so vegetarian coverage should be confirmed directly with the business.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Active, open pub explicitly welcoming Galloping Goose Trail cyclists; confirmed operating with current website and matched contact details.
enrichment_extras.notes: Homepage text 'just hopping off the Galloping Goose Trail' is strong evidence this is a cyclist-aware establishment; worth highlighting in any directory blurb.

Vegetarian / vegan / GF.detail: Multiple menu items marked '(V)', including Cauliflower Bites and Classic Poutine; note that (V) appears inconsistently on some meat-containing dishes as well
